headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and MCP interaction: Windsurf can overwrite Prefect-driven artifacts, enabling prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf exposes clipboard, workspace files, and MCP servers, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content from shared artifacts. Prefect has broad network egress and API access, so if it writes workflow outputs into the same workspace, those outputs can be re-read as instructions. The shared filesystem bridge makes injection plausible even without a documented direct channel.
conditions: IF Prefect writes untrusted workflow output into a workspace file that Windsurf opens
IF Windsurf reads clipboard or MCP content originating from Prefect-managed artifacts
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Store Prefect outputs in a separate directory from Windsurf workspaces
Require manual review before Windsurf opens Prefect-generated files
Turn off MCP servers for sessions that process untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress; Windsurf reads open files and workspace files and can also use MCP servers. If both share a local workspace, source code or open files can flow from Windsurf into Prefect-managed outputs or external APIs. The profiles do not prove secret handling, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local workspace
IF Prefect sends workflow contents to external APIs while Windsurf has open source files in that workspace
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Restrict Prefect runs to non-sensitive workflow metadata
Pause Windsurf before opening confidential files
Disable automatic file syncing between editor sessions
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared directories

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via local filesystem across instances. Prefect can also affect files through orchestration outputs and broad network-driven automation. In a shared repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking, making destructive conflicts plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF Prefect and Windsurf target the same repository or directory
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while Prefect writes generated artifacts into that tree
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones
Disable Windsurf auto-execute for shared repos
Serialize writes with a lock file
Commit Prefect outputs on a dedicated branch
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s Cascade loop can act on file contents and tool outputs, while Prefect can generate workflow artifacts that Windsurf may treat as authoritative. If Prefect emits incorrect metadata or code, Windsurf can propagate it into edits, shell commands, or git commits without a verification gate. That creates a strong cascading-error pathway with potentially irreversible changes.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes Prefect-generated files as inputs to Cascade
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled or the operator approves commands without review
mitigations: Require human review of Prefect outputs before Windsurf acts on them
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Add a validation step between Prefect and Windsurf
Use read-only handoff files for intermediate artifacts
requires-engineering: implement schema checks on Prefect outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch. The only concrete compliance concern is that Windsurf handles model provider keys and open files, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and broad egress, so a policy gap could arise if regulated data is placed in shared workflows. The evidence is insufficient for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Prefect workflow metadata or Windsurf open files
IF organizational policy forbids model-provider-key handling in the same workspace as regulated data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Separate secrets from workspace files
Review retention settings for both tools
Document which data classes each agent may touch
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for sensitive workspaces
